title: A closed subset meeting the generic fibre meets all nearby fibres
statement: Let h:P\to T be finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let eta be a generic point of all of T, and let C be a closed subset of P. If C intersect h^{-1}({eta}) is nonempty, there is an open V containing eta such that C intersect h^{-1}({t}) is nonempty for every t in V. The set-theoretic fibres agree with the images of the scheme fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. No noetherianity, reducedness, or separatedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 055G, nonempty-intersection image argument; Tags 052A and 01UA.

proof.text: Construct the reduced induced closed subscheme of C explicitly using Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal. Its inclusion i has range C and is a closed immersion. Put f=i followed by h. The map j:T.nilradical.subscheme to T is a surjective closed embedding, hence a homeomorphism, by support_nilradical and range_subschemeι. Lift eta along j. Specialization reflection by the embedding proves the lift is generic, so the reduced base is irreducible and therefore integral. All of these constructions and properties use the existing proved Mathlib and WeilConjectures ideal-sheaf API.

The closed subscheme of C is reduced, so f.liftNilradical gives an explicit morphism g to the reduced base with g followed by j equal to f. Finite type descends to g by locallyOfFiniteType_of_comp; quasi-compactness descends by QuasiCompact.of_comp since j is a closed immersion and therefore quasi-separated. Apply generic flatness with local finite presentation to g.

Every nonempty open of the reduced base contains the lifted generic point. Lift the point of C over eta to the closed subscheme, using the range equality. Injectivity of j shows its image under g is the lifted generic point. This point therefore belongs to the range of the restricted map.

The flat locally finitely presented restricted map is open by Mathlib UniversallyOpen.of_flat (Tag 01UA). Its range is open in U, its image under U.ι is open in the reduced base, and its image under the homeomorphism j is open in T and contains eta. For any point in this image, unwind the two image witnesses and the range witness. The corresponding point in the closed subscheme maps to a point of C in the requested fibre, by g followed by j equals i followed by h.

proof_origin.note: Lean proof by M1 follows this route, using reduced-source liftNilradical in place of pulling back P and C. All glue is proved; only the full generic-flatness clause is split off.
